narrative.overview: Mawqifi is a wayfinding plate, not a map. It borrows the grammar of a printed campus board: a chalk ground, a warm paper plate, pine enamel for institutional ink, hairline rules, square tick marks, and numbers large enough to read at arm's length. The interface answers which stop, how far, when — and then shows its work. The user picked this direction from three cards; it replaces an indigo product-sheet direction with something rooted in place.
keyCharacteristics: Chalk ground and warm plate; no gradients, glass, photography or fake texture.
Pine is institutional ink; orange is reserved for estimates, attention and focus.
Changa for display and numbers, Readex Pro for reading; tabular digits.
Square geometry: 0px radii, 1px rules, 8–9px nodes, 50×54 stop tabs.
Signature: the measured rule with three facts and a provenance line under each.
Arabic-first RTL, Western tabular digits, bidi isolation for times and Latin tokens.

rules.name: The Earned Orange Rule
rules.body: Orange appears only when the interface is estimating, warning, or focused. If a screen has no estimate, no attention state and no focus, it has no orange.

rules.name: The One Ground Rule
rules.body: The page is chalk. No gradient washes, glass panels, photographic textures or a second field color; depth comes from a hairline and one low shadow.

rules.name: The Institutional Ink Rule
rules.body: Pine is authority, not success. Do not use it for valid, live or confirmed states.

rules.name: The Tabular Measure Rule
rules.body: Times, distances, stop numbers and counts use tabular numerals. Changa digits are a uniform 0.5em, so 07:30 and 08:00 align without a mono face.

rules.name: The Printed Sheet Rule
rules.body: A surface earns a shadow only if it is a sheet of paper on the board. Do not add shadows to buttons, chips, rows or the direction switch.

dos: Do put provenance in the same viewport as the number: a node on the rule, a source line under the value, and a note under the facts.
Do keep the three facts side by side at 320px; shorten labels rather than stacking the table.
Do use dir="ltr" and tabular numerals for times, margins and Latin tokens inside the RTL page.
Do keep tappable controls at 44×44 or larger with a visible 2px focus ring.
donts: Don't add pills, rounded cards, gradients, glassmorphism or a second ground color.
Don't use orange as a link color, a decorative accent or a success badge.
Don't invent an arrival time, a walking minute or a stop number to fill a column; missing is an outlined node and an em dash.
Don't put a whole live region around the plate; announce a concise state summary.
Don't let measured values flicker on every render; honor prefers-reduced-motion.
